page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.2-8 is an x86_64 virtual machine configuration within the flexible Standard3 family. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8358 processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.6 GHz. It is provisioned with 4 virtual CPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory is configured at 8.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

The architecture does not bundle local disk storage, operating with zero local NVMe or SSD capacity, which necessitates the use of remote network-attached block volumes for persistent filesystems and the operating system. Graphic acceleration is not present, with 0 GPUs provisioned. The configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because virtual CPUs are backed by dedicated physical cores, execution performance avoids hypervisor-level credit mechanisms or contention with unrelated tenant workloads.

Given its 1:2 compute-to-memory density and dedicated Intel architecture, VM.Standard3.Flex.2-8 offers predictable resource allocation for CPU-centric tasks with moderate memory demands. Practical workload fits include containerized microservices, continuous integration build nodes, lightweight API gateways, batch processing scripts, and general web application tiers.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.2-8 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8358 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, the instance allocates 2 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core, yielding a focused 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per thread. This instance type contains no integrated GPUs and includes no local storage, requiring remote network-attached block storage for operating system and application data persistence. One complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the deployment. With its dedicated processor allocation and lean memory envelope, VM.Standard3.Flex.2-8 provides a predictable compute foundation suitable for containerized microservices, distributed API backends, continuous integration build jobs, batch processing routines, and standard web serving workloads that do not demand extensive in-memory caching.
